Consonantal i

Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

card game noun and phrase

also play cards, cards (the game), game of cards

modern

Traupman 51

lūdus chartulārum

Traupman’s chartulārum (lūsōriārum) lūdus, after his chartula lūsōria for the card itself (see playing card).

Other words

  • chartulīs lūdere — play cards

    modern · Traupman 51; Andresian p. 16

    The ablative of the thing played with, as in pilā lūdere, tālīs lūdere (Cic. Sen. 58).

  • lūdus chartārum

    also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. card game, from Vives 1540

    With chartīs lūdere, “play cards”: Vives’s words.

  • lūdus foliōrum

    also used · Renaissance · M-O s.v. card game, from Vives 1540

    Vives’s other word, from folium lūsōrium, a playing card; with foliīs lūsitāre, “play cards”.

Examples

  • Adfer, quaesō, folia lūsōria, quae inveniēs sub abacō ad sinistram.

    Bring the playing cards, please: you’ll find them under the sideboard on the left.Vīv. Exerc. 6

  • Vīn’ chartulīs lūdāmus?

    Shall we play cards?composed

See also playing card, deal, shuffle, dealer, hand, suit.
